RQ1.rationale: The paper centrally addresses general CubeSat mission/system modeling via a reusable SysML reference model, though not a detailed EPS behavior model.

RQ2.rationale: It claims system-level reuse, quality, traceability, common-baseline, and adoption outcomes attributed to MBSE/CSRM, but not measured EPS reliability or reproducibility outcomes.

RQ3.rationale: The CSRM includes generic model-linked V&V activities and technical measures before physical development, but no EPS-specific verification procedures, SIL/HIL, or test results.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Part of the INCOSE SSWG CubeSat/RAX MBSE lineage: earlier phases developed a SysML CubeSat/RAX model, added downlink and power-usage behaviors, and integrated MagicDraw/Cameo, ModelCenter/MBSE Analyzer, STK, and MATLAB for trade studies. Treat lineage evidence as related, not independent replication.

lightweight_resource_constrained_tailori.rationale: The model targets university CubeSat teams and generic/loosely defined CubeSat subsystems, but does not measure lightweight adoption effort.

governance_project_deliverables_roi.rationale: OMG process/conformance and generic buy-offs/design reviews/specifications are discussed; ROI and concrete project-deliverable evidence are not reported.

newspace_agile_distributed_rapid_iterati.rationale: No NewSpace, agile, distributed-team, concurrent-design, or rapid-iteration process is discussed.

RQ1: The paper provides a CubeSat mission/system reference model in SysML organized around stakeholders, requirements, behaviors, architecture, technical measures, and V&V.
Generalization is achieved through a platform-independent reference model, reusable library of elements, generic/loosely defined subsystems, and methodology-agnostic population guidance.
EPS is not modeled in detail; power appears as a generic subsystem and in lineage-level power trade-study history.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include reuse, quality enhancement, development-time reduction, common baseline comparison, institutional knowledge transfer, traceability, and standards/reusable-library potential.

Evidence is mostly qualitative: formal review, university use, model-structure figures, and historical trade-study mentions; no quantitative EPS reliability/reproducibility/integrability evidence is reported.
The strongest synthesis-relevant evidence is structural traceability and reported vetting/use, not measured project performance.
RQ3: The CSRM includes validation and verification packages and activity elements that can capture plans, procedures, execution notes/results/status and link to requirements, objectives, and technical measures.
Pre-physical verification is conceptual/model-structural and generic rather than an EPS-specific procedure or executable check in this paper.
No EPS test procedures, verification matrix, SIL/HIL, hardware integration, or flight evidence are presented.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: The CSRM is targeted especially at university CubeSat mission architecture teams and is not methodology-specific.
Teams determine which model elements and relationships to use and may modify the containment tree to fit their methodology.
Feedback from university teams will be evaluated for inclusion, including value-added elements not currently in the CSRM, portions that do not function as intended, and new capabilities.
Dissemination/control/update processes and formats for a possible OMG specification have yet to be worked out.
Expansion from CubeSats to broader satellite classes is future work.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No dedicated EPS model, EPS requirement set, power modes/loads, EPS verification procedure, or EPS test evidence.
Claims about development time, quality, economies, reuse, and common baseline lack metrics, baselines, and effect sizes.
Model file, version, license, repository, current tool instance, and exchange formats are not provided.
Vetting and university-use claims lack evaluation criteria, detailed feedback, and outcome data.
No hardware/software integration, operational, or flight evidence for CSRM benefits.
Lineage overlap with prior RAX/CSRM publications should be accounted for in synthesis.

direct_evidence_quotes_for_classificatio.quote: The CubeSat System Reference Model (CSRM) is a representation of the logical architecture of a CubeSat System, intended to be used by system architects and engineers as a starting point
The CSRM is a SysML compliant and platform-independent model that provides building blocks that can be specialized to support CubeSat mission design.
This reusable model supports reducing development times and increasing the quality of CubeSat spacecraft and ground system design
tracing requirements from stakeholders, behaviors, and technical measures down to subsystems and components and then to validation and verification activities
The CubeSat subsystems are generically and loosely defined as a starting point for the mission specific CubeSat team.
The Verification Activity element describes the process for verifying an element, e.g. a requirement.
what formats will be available have yet to be worked out

synthesis_consistency.notes_for_consistency_with_lineage: Treat this as the 2020 CSRM/reference-model paper, not as independent evidence of the RAX executable simulation trade-study results reported in earlier lineage papers. EPS coding should remain adjacent/weak unless the synthesis specifically uses lineage-level power trade-study mentions.
synthesis_consistency.extraction_confidence_reason: The paper text and figure descriptions are sufficiently complete for system-level CSRM extraction; most classifications are directly quote-supported and absent EPS/outcome evidence is explicit.
